newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease, more losses seen.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease, more losses seen.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased on Monday, extending their losses to a third trading session on meagre turnover.
Traders blamed the inactivity to a stark absence of fresh buying incentives and said the blue-chip SBI index would likely continue falling over the medium term.
The SBI index fell 0.43 percent or 5.62 points to 1,303.56. Overall 10 shares fell, four rose and three were flat, while 11 were untraded. Turnover rose to 39.1 million tolars from 36.3 million.
"I expect the status quo on our market to persist until the end of the summer, pushing the SBI index even under 1,200 points," said Klara Zupancic, a trader at bank SKB.
Market participants said Tuesday's session could receive a boost if shopping centre operator BTC lists its global depository receipts (GDRs) abroad.

"There are rumours on the market that BTC will list its GDRs on the London and New York bourses later today, so tommorow's trading could be influenced significantly by the listing," said Predrag Stamenkovic of brokers BPH.
No one at the company was available for immediate comment on the listing, but BTC said it would hold a news conference on the subject on Tuesday at 0800 GMT.
BTC, which completed a roadshow for the GDR issue last week, would be the second Slovenian company to be listed abroad after bank SKB.
"I expect the BTC price here to differ by 20 percent from the London price, if nothing special happens the BTC price could move between 13,000 and 18,000 tolars," Stamenkovic said.
Issue A of drug maker Lek was the most active, firming 0.17 percent to 24,180 tolars on volume of 603 shares for total turnover of 14.6 million tolars.
Preferred shares of Dolenjska bank led the day's decliner, falling 3.52 percent to 13,990 tolars on volume of 200 shares.
"I can see no particular reason for today's fall in the bank, it is most probably just a reflection of the general falling trend that is going on on our market," Stamenkovic added.
Bank UBK was the top gainer, jumping 8.54 percent to 8,900 tolars on volume of only one share.

Since April 29, when UBK announced it would link up with Slovenia's second largest bank SKB, UBK's shares have jumped 41.3 percent, but traders said today's jump was not significant as only one share was traded. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
